newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa foreign debt bill to soar in 1997 - paper.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa foreign debt bill to soar in 1997 - paper.

text.p: South Africa's long-term foreign debt falling due next year would be about $1.1 billion more than this year at about $2.9 billion rand, the Business Day newspaper reported on Friday.

The increase, due to the first repayments of South Africa's loans from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) which begin in March next year, could put severe pressure on the country's foreign exchange reserves.
The paper quoted economists saying the quarterly payment of $100 million for eight consecutive quarters could also sway government to make use of IMF facilities again.
They said $6.05 billion in short-term debt would have to be repaid next year, with a further $2.9 billion in long-term debt adding to the pressure.

While short-term amounts were easily rolled over and usually related to trade financing, long-term debts might not be refinanced so easily and if there was not enough compensating capital inflows, the country could find its reserves severely depleted.
South Africa's gross gold and foreign exchange reserves stood at 10.935 billion rand in November, up from 10.284 billion rand in October.
